record.tranche_reason: The paper studies grokking on modular arithmetic with a single-hidden-layer MLP. It does not test the listed CIFAR benchmarks, depth and shortcut effects, initialization comparisons, learning-rate stability, or batch-normalization effects.
record.gate_note: The paper reports modular-task generalization and feature-learning results. Those do not test the listed claim versions. It also describes training-loss dynamics without reporting training classification-error values for the listed settings.
record.test_reason: The study reports grokking and feature learning in single-hidden-layer MLPs on modular arithmetic. Its own results do not test any listed version: width results concern test accuracy rather than spurious minima, and optimizer comparisons concern grokking time rather than learning-rate stability or a controlled batch-normalization effect.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors demonstrate grokking in single-hidden-layer MLPs under vanilla gradient descent with MSE and no explicit regularization, derive task-solving periodic representations for a class of modular functions, and show that optimization finds similar representations. They report that adaptive methods and regularization improve grokking speed and data efficiency.
record.recipe_differences: Single-hidden-layer MLP on modular arithmetic with MSE loss; the paper does not use the benchmark and architecture settings in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Grokking depends on modular function, training-data fraction and sampling, width, optimizer, and regularization; the paper says some functions do not generalize or do not reach 100% test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Training loss decreases slowly before either settling into memorization or accelerating during grokking and periodic-feature formation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Modular-task MLPs can show delayed generalization associated with learning task-specific periodic features.

record.problems: The reported general training-loss dynamics provide no numerical training classification-error values. Some results are presented only in figures, and the text notes that grokking time near the critical data fraction is difficult to determine.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying result rows for the listed versions. Generalization-accuracy and analytic-solution results were left out because they do not report training classification error or test a listed version.

untested.parts: Training classification error in large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels and effects of size, early stopping, or regularization.
Spurious local minima in ReLU teacher-student problems and their reduction by adding student neurons.
Training degradation with depth, identity shortcuts, and the specified alternative training recipes.
Initialization comparisons affecting signal propagation, training speed, and trainable depth. The analytic task-solving weights are not an initialization experiment.
Learning rates relative to stability thresholds, curvature dynamics, recovery, and divergence.
Controlled batch-normalization comparisons for training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup. Trying SGD with Batchnorm does not establish these effects.

record.verdict_notes: Failure to generalize on difficult modular functions does not establish failure to fit training data. Neither those results nor the width-dependent accuracy of constructed analytic solutions bears on the listed optimization versions.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/100, convolutional networks, corrupted or random labels, and comparisons involving size, early stopping, and regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Depth comparisons, batch-normalized convolutional networks, identity shortcuts, and the cited special training recipes.
Comparisons of initialization schemes and their effects on signal propagation, training speed, or trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, curvature or sharpness dynamics, recovery, and divergence.
Batch-normalization comparisons and Fixup training results.
